Step 2: Functional validation (2026-02-23) — model parity checks vs internal baseline for clinical prompts

Step 4: Soak test (2026-02-24 to 2026-02-26) — 48-hour sustained run to observe memory leaks, heat saturation, KV cache behavior

performance_targets: Chat (512 token avg): p95 latency <= 120ms, p99 <= 220ms under sustained load
Embeddings batch: throughput >= 1500 vectors/s per cluster during peak
Sustained throughput target for POC: 2k RPS for small chat queries with autoscale disabled (reserved capacity)
reserved_gpu_plan: Initial baseline: reserve 6 x H100 nodes (customer prefers H100 for FP16+quant workflows)
Scale plan: ability to add 6 more nodes as burst capacity or on short lead with 30-day notice
Goal: fixed monthly commit covering baseline, with burst billing for excess usage
sla_negotiation_points: Define p99 and p95 latency SLOs with credits for missed targets (formula proposed by AE)
Clarify scheduled maintenance windows and notification windows (aim <= 4 per year, < 2 hours each)
Incident response SLA: 1-hour P1 acknowledgement, 4-hour mitigation plan
Data residency guarantee for EU subset with attestations and audit logs
Explicit definitions around 'downtime' vs 'degraded performance' for credits
requirements_summary: Seeking Dedicated capacity for latency-sensitive HealthTech inference: chat and reranking during clinic hours, embeddings for nightly indexing. Must support private VPC deployment with on-prem option for PHI, SOC2/ISO27001 compliance, KMS integration, and EU residency for a subset. Performance goals: predictable p95/p99 tail latencies under sustained reserved loads; reserved GPU plan must be clear and contractable. Legal needs SLA language on credits, maintenance, and incident response. POC includes load and soak tests using representative clinical prompts and anonymized documents.
